research_question: Is the larger g8 reference-to-Q.ANT logit error explained by accumulation of amplitude-weighted component residuals rather than by high Fourier frequencies alone?
observations: Exp018 falsified the simple high-frequency explanation: replacing frequencies 5-8 with repeated frequencies 1-4 did not reduce logit MAE.
Q.ANT KAN output is a sum of amplitude-weighted periodic components, so deployment residuals can accumulate or cancel according to learned amplitude magnitude and sign.
g8 has twice as many trainable Fourier components as g4 and Exp017 measured substantially larger model-level logit error.
hypothesis: Compared with g4, standard g8 will exhibit larger amplitude-weighted accumulated component residual at the output, and this accumulated residual will explain its larger reference-to-Q.ANT logit error better than frequency identity alone.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if g8 does not have larger accumulated amplitude-weighted component residual than g4, or if the reconstructed component-residual sum does not closely track the observed reference-to-Q.ANT logit error.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The component decomposition is diagnostic and does not itself prove that amplitude regularization will improve accuracy.
The test subset is limited to 1000 examples to keep component-level Q.ANT evaluation tractable.
